entry.title: General-purpose equations of state for hadron-quark matter: first application to accretion-induced phase transitions in neutron stars
entry.summary: Strong first-order phase transitions in the cores of neutron stars (NSs) can have profound implications for astrophysical observables, however, their existence remains an open question. Since most NSs form in binary systems, they are expected to experience prolonged episodes of mass accretion that gradually increase their central density and can potentially trigger such a transition. This might, in turn, generate observable multi-messenger signals, as suggested by previous studies. Motivated by this prospect, we generate a new set of equations of state for hadron--quark matter with first-order phase transitions of various strengths, including neutrino absorption opacities in the quark phase as well. We then perform general-relativistic radiation hydrodynamics simulations of NSs undergoing accretion-induced phase transitions. In contrast to previous findings, our results indicate that these systems do not produce unbound ejecta for the models considered, making accretion-induced phase transitions unlikely sources of observable electromagnetic transients. However, we find that transitions are accompanied by intense neutrino emission, with peak luminosities reaching $\sim10^{52}~\mathrm{erg/s}$ for the strongest transition considered. To facilitate future numerical studies, we make the family of equations of state and neutrino opacities used in this work publicly available, enabling the systematic exploration of the role of the phase transition strength.

entry.title: Collinear Gluons from Gravity: Poincaré-Birkhoff-Witt Decomposition and Twisted Intersections
entry.summary: We give an explicit reconstruction of subleading collinear Yang--Mills amplitudes from one-graviton amplitudes in Einstein--Yang--Mills theory and its string corrections. We realize the monodromy kernel in the mixed open-closed string relation as a weighted Lie-algebraic recursion on words of gluon labels. At order $α'^r$, its output contains at most $r$ Lie factors. The Poincaré--Birkhoff--Witt (PBW) theorem decomposes the space spanned by gluon orderings into sectors whose dimensions are given by unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind. Appropriate shuffle sums of one-graviton amplitudes extract the degree-$r$ sector, for which the string-period matrix drops out. Accordingly, we show that the reconstruction coefficients factor into linear kinematic factors over the product of bipartition factors. Finally, we express the reconstruction coefficients as twisted intersection numbers between Parke--Taylor forms and explicit forest cocycles constructed recursively from logarithmic four-point differentials.

entry.title: Finding CFTs from spatial positivity of partition functions
entry.summary: We discuss a positivity property for partition functions that generalizes modular invariance and which is here conjectured to hold for general 2D CFTs. We show its relation to positivity properties of Rényi entropies and its meaning in terms of topological defect lines. We apply the conjecture to find consistent local unitary CFT models which are not necessarily modular invariant.

entry.title: Reentrant $d=2+1$ Superfluidity at High Temperature
entry.summary: We present a UV-complete model with a global $U(1)$ symmetry in $d=2+1$ dimensions that exhibits a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) ordered phase at arbitrarily high temperatures. A careful separation of scales yields a two-dimensional Euclidean effective field theory whose construction remains perturbatively controlled even when its soft modes become strongly coupled. We determine the BKT phase boundary by carefully matching this theory to existing lattice Monte Carlo results. The high-temperature phase supports gapless static modes and algebraically decaying correlations even as $T\to\infty$.

entry.title: Twisted scattering from Chern-Simons theory
entry.summary: We consider boundary conditions of two-dimensional Dirac fermions which preserve a non-anomalous continuous symmetry which acts differently on the left- and right-movers. Such boundaries are equivalent to topological defects of Weyl fermions preserving the symmetry. We give a general construction of such defects for conformally-embedded symmetries using Chern-Simons theory. They always exist and can be realised as half-space gauging defects for some finite categorical symmetry. Using this technology, we compute the twist lines to which fermions become attached upon scattering through the defect, the boundary central charge of the corresponding folded boundary state, and its mod-2 valued SPT class. As applications, we first consider abelian symmetries and find agreement with known results in the literature. We then study a novel example where an $SU(2) \times SU(4) \times U(1)^2$ symmetry is preserved. In contrast to the abelian case, the twist lines are intrinsically non-invertible and belong to either a $\text{TY}(\mathbb{Z}_3 \times \mathbb{Z}_3)$ or $\text{Rep}(\mathbb{S}_3) \times \mathbb{Z}_3$ symmetry depending on whether scattering is to the left or the right.

entry.title: A signature of the timelike singularity in holography
entry.summary: In the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence, we provide a simple observable, the imaginary part of the retarded Green's function, which captures the timelike singularity of a charged black brane. Solving wave equations of bulk fields with different spins outside the black brane, we calculate exponentially small contributions to retarded Green's functions in the dual CFT at large real frequency. These contributions admit an interpretation in terms of paths in an analytically continued classical black brane interior via a WKB approximation: they provide the complex time elapsed along null geodesics that reflect off the singularity, and incorporate the corresponding reflection coefficients.

entry.title: Optimal galaxy magnification: generalized fundamental-plane residuals and number counts are all you need
entry.summary: Weak-lensing magnification complements cosmic shear through its effects on galaxy fluxes, sizes, and number counts. We derive the optimal magnification statistics from galaxy properties and show that the optimal measurement can be decomposed into an optimal mean statistic and total number counts. The optimal mean statistic can be constructed from the residual distribution of a generalized fundamental plane (GFP), $F(i,\boldsymbol{X})$, which predicts galaxy size or, equivalently, flux from surface brightness $i$ and additional lensing-invariant properties $\boldsymbol{X}$. The function $F$ can take any form that reduces the intrinsic scatter and thereby improves magnification precision. For a Gaussian residual distribution, the optimal mean statistic reduces to the inverse-variance-weighted residual, or simply the residual for constant scatter. Together with total number counts, this statistic captures all the magnification Fisher information under Poisson statistics, achieving the same precision as a full-likelihood analysis. This provides a simple and physically intuitive optimal compression of the full magnification likelihood, avoiding the need to model the potentially high-dimensional galaxy-property distribution, particularly when additional observables are incorporated to reduce the GFP scatter. Our results demonstrate that GFP residuals and number counts provide an optimal combination for weak-lensing magnification measurements in galaxy surveys.

entry.title: Phonon-assisted free-electron recoil control and mechanical sensing
entry.summary: Mechanical vibrations are fundamental to a wide range of physical phenomena and technologies, yet their ability to actively shape free-electron dynamics remains largely unexplored. Here we theoretically show how an optomechanical membrane provides a phonon-assisted optical interface for controlling free-electron recoil and sensing localized forces. Transverse membrane motion scatters cavity light into high-momentum evanescent sidebands that enable phase-matched interaction with electrons traveling in vacuum. Beyond supplying momentum for phase matching, the vibration amplitude controls the electron-light interaction strength and redistributes electron populations among recoil orders. External forces that perturb the vibration are thereby encoded in the electron recoil spectrum. Under the modeled conditions, electron readout of localized stochastic forces can yield a higher signal-to-noise ratio than a Gaussian optical homodyne benchmark at equal detected probe rates. These results provide a theoretical basis for mechanically reconfigurable free-electron optics and mode-selective mechanical sensing.

entry.title: On Particle Production from Bubble Collisions in the Non-runaway Regime
entry.summary: Particle production from bubble collisions during First-Order Phase Transitions (FOPTs) has been studied as an efficient mechanism for baryogenesis and dark matter production, but existing semi-analytical treatments assume runaway bubbles with wall velocity $v_w\to 1$. We generalize this treatment to arbitrary $v_w< 1$, relevant for scenarios such as electroweak baryogenesis and transitions with significant wall friction. We first extend the analytical trapping-equation approach to finite-thickness boosted kink profiles for both elastic and inelastic collisions, then go beyond this by numerically solving the full Klein-Gordon equation without assuming $SO(1,1)$ symmetry or thin walls, across a broad grid of $v_w$ and potential shapes. We find the analytical generalization underestimates the true efficiency factor by orders of magnitude away from $v_w\to 1$, and provide new semi-analytic fit functions consisting of a power-law continuum plus a resonance peak, which reproduce the main spectral features of the numerical results across the parameter range studied. Applying these to a toy dark sector model, we show particle production is strongly suppressed as $v_w$ decreases from unity, enhanced for lighter produced particles, and that the relative contribution from the oscillatory peak differs from prior runaway-regime estimates. We also discuss limitations of the trapping equation and the off-shell effective-action truncation underlying this formalism.

entry.title: Modeling MAD Sgr A* flares and their dependence on spin
entry.summary: Aims: This study aims to place constraints on the spin of Sgr A* from recent flare observations. It models the flare kinematics in the vicinity of a supermassive black hole, evaluates their dependence on black hole spin, and assesses the correlation between the spin of the black hole and the astrometric observations in the Galactic center. Methods: Our study extends the work of Antonopoulou et al. 2025 to a range of black hole spins. A prominent flux eruption is identified in the simulation, and the evolution of the active region on the equatorial plane is tracked during the event. The flare model consists of a spherical hot spot ejected along the flux tube with a relativistic velocity. Results: In MAD simulations, the flux tube wraps around the jet funnel in the opposite direction to the black hole's spin. This dependence is imprinted on the flare trajectory and provides a strong correlation between the spin of the black and the flare kinematics. This analysis favors Kerr black holes, with a preference towards larger spin magnitude. Although prograde simulations show a consistent clockwise motion in the sky regardless of disk rotation, retrograde models require a clockwise accretion disk to account for the observations of July 22, 2018. Conclusions: A maximally rotating Kerr black hole is the most promising candidate for reproducing the observed flare trajectory in the vicinity of Sgr A*, illustrating a pass faction surpassing $90\%$ among the investigated flare models. In particular, determining spin orientation within this model is linked to the rotation of the accretion disk. Assuming a counterclockwise accretion disk, a prograde black hole with $a\geq1/2$ is able to reproduce the observed flare kinematics in the Galactic center. Conversely, assuming a clockwise rotation for the disk, the observations support both prograde and retrograde Kerr black holes with a large spin.

entry.title: Extended vs. thin screen approximation in astrophysical settings
entry.summary: Context: In the context of radio wave propagation through plasma concentrations and for gravitational lensing, the thin screen approximation often provides a suitable approximation for scattering and deflections caused by three-dimensional spatial structures. For scattering of electromagnetic waves from an extended medium, stochastic theories provide analytical bounds on ensemble averaged quantities, such as the scintillation index. If neither the conditions for a stochastic treatment nor the thin screen approximation are fulfilled, fully numerical methods are required. Aims: For an extended structure, the applicability of the thin screen approximation needs to be verified by comparing it with the fully three-dimensional scattering solution. We discuss various exact solutions to simple lensing geometries and provide numerical results for the propagation in the branched-flow regime, which is also of relevance in astrophysical applications. Methods: We transfer several analytical results obtained in quantum mechanical scattering theory to astrophysical settings and complement them with different numerical methods to quantify the deviations of thin screen theories from an extended medium results. Results: We provide the analytical results for spherical waves scattered by a point source and show the emergence of branchef flow in the intermediate regime between thin screen physics and stochastic media results.

entry.title: AnyonWiki.org
entry.summary: The AnyonWiki is an open-source project that provides full algebraic and numerical data of fusion and unitary modular fusion categories as a resource for the scientific community. It comes with a database, the AnyonWikiDatabase, that currently includes the classification of multiplicity-free pivotal (braided) fusion categories through rank 7 and more than 25000 fusion rings including the classification of multiplicity-free fusion rings through rank 10, with work in progress to expand. This data is available through AnyonWiki.org, a website that provides robust search and download functionality and presents each fusion ring and category via a dedicated webpage. In this short article we discuss the data available at AnyonWiki.org as well as the scientific and communal motivations for the design of its underlying AnyonWikiDatabase, which are centered around making the data accessible, independently verifiable, granularly citable, useful, and easy to work with.

entry.title: Wormhole geometries and energy conditions in linear and non-linear $f(Q,L_m)$ gravity
entry.summary: This study explores static and spherically symmetric wormhole configurations in an extended formulation of symmetric teleparallel gravity governed by $f(Q,L_m)=α(-Q)+βL_m $ and $f(Q,L_m)= -Q+L_m^α $ (where $Q$ is the non-metricity scalar, $L_m$ is the matter Lagrangian, and $α, β$ are constants). By varying the action with respect to the metric, we obtain the corresponding field equations. We conclude that the linear $f(Q,L_m)=α(-Q)+βL_m$ framework successfully supports physically realistic wormholes without requiring extreme energy condition violations. It has been demonstrated that spacetime solutions violating both the radial and lateral null energy conditions in general relativity can nevertheless satisfy the NEC in $f(Q, L_m)$ gravity. Within non-linear $f(Q,L_m)$ gravity, non-exotic asymptotically flat wormhole solutions are derived using linear and asymptotically linear equations of state. Our results open new avenues to link modified gravity models with the observable astrophysical traits of exotic spacetimes.

entry.title: Inaccessibility of the Cosmological Singularity to Quantum Probes
entry.summary: We propose an operational resolution of the FLRW big bang singularity using quantum probes satisfying a curvature coupled Klein-Gordon equation. Applying the Madelung-Bohm decomposition of a Klein-Gordon field on a classical near-singularity FLRW background, we show that the induced conformal geometry renders curvature invariants finite and makes past directed causal geodesics complete. The classical big bang surface is therefore inaccessible to this class of quantum probes in finite effective proper time, while the underlying FLRW spacetime remains singular.

entry.title: Anisotropy and tracer-profile assumptions in aperture-based strong-lens dynamics: Conditional inference from supernova distance ratios and unresolved stellar kinematics
entry.summary: Single-aperture stellar kinematics jointly constrain the mass distribution, tracer light profile, and velocity anisotropy. Their coupling affects the interpretation of an inferred anisotropy. We quantify how tracer-profile assumptions and data treatment affect common-anisotropy comparisons and inferred mass-density slopes in a compiled galaxy-scale lens sample. We analyse 107 lenses using distinct \pantheon\ supernova counterparts, spatial flatness, distance duality, and the full supernova covariance. We compare the individual-slope power-law tracer with Hernquist and Sérsic profiles using measured effective radii. Numerical Jeans solutions, likelihood comparisons, posterior distributions, and controlled recovery experiments quantify the effects of tracer representation. The power-law fixed-minus-free Bayesian information criterion differences are 6.74 for isotropy and 41.51 for fixed $β=0.18$, compared with $-3.89$ and $-2.26$ for Hernquist and $-4.67$ and $-4.30$ for Sérsic $n=4$. The preference also changes with Sérsic index. Removing 12 systems with linearised distance-ratio uncertainty above 20\% reduces the power-law isotropy comparison to 2.51. In isotropic Sérsic $n=4$ and Hernquist simulations, power-law fits yield $Δ\mathrm{BIC}_0>6$ in 60.0\% and 50.0\% of realisations, respectively, compared with 0.5\% and 1.0\% for matched-tracer fits.} {The preference for a common free anisotropy parameter depends on the tracer representation and sample composition. Controlled recovery identifies tracer mismatch as one mechanism that can generate this preference within the adopted aperture models. Physical interpretation requires joint treatment of photometry, distance uncertainties, and kinematic weighting.

entry.title: Hydrodynamic description of correlation matrix eigenvalues in a finite temperature expanding free fermionic gas
entry.summary: A recent work considered the Page curve for entanglement entropy of a freely expanding one-dimensional Fermi gas starting from a finite box (the system) in a zero-temperature initial state that then expands in to a semi-infinite vacuum (the environment). For the case with a single defect at the system-environment junction, it was shown that the Yang-Yang entropy of the system computed from semiclassical hydrodynamics agrees with the microscopically computed entanglement entropy, yielding the Page curve. On the other hand, the environment Yang-Yang entropy showed a monotonic increase. Here, we propose a hydrodynamic description to obtain the eigenvalues of the microscopic correlation matrix for a nonzero temperature freely-expanding Fermi gas. For the system, the phase space density directly gives the correlation matrix eigenvalues and thus, via the Yang-Yang formula, yields the von-Neumann entropy. For the reservoir, a modification of the phase space density is required in the Yang-Yang formula, to incorporate coherences, in order to reproduce accurately the entropy. The hydrodynamic description of correlation matrix eigenvalues also leads to a Levitov-Lesovik type formula for the full-counting-statistics for a finite system in the transient regime. We provide a heuristic derivation of the correlation matrix eigenvalues based on a semiclassical wave-packet picture.

entry.title: High-fidelity and robust controlled-Z gates for superconducting transmon qubits. I. Intrinsic errors and decoherence
entry.summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires quantum gates that combine short duration, high fidelity, and robustness to noise. As quantum processors scale, robustness becomes increasingly important because exhaustive characterization and frequent recalibration of individual gates become impractical. We present a comprehensive optimal-control framework for controlled-Z (CZ) gates between directly coupled, frequency-tunable transmons that systematically accounts for intrinsic Hamiltonian errors and realistic decoherence mechanisms, including energy relaxation and dephasing. Using smooth, single-shot flux pulses, we obtain 12-ns CZ gates---close to the theoretical speed limit of 11.6 ns---with intrinsic errors suppressed to the $2\times10^{-5}$ level. We construct dephasing noise models, calibrated against published experimental measurements, that capture fast dephasing from room-temperature control electronics and slow dephasing from $1/f$ flux noise. Using these models, we identify dephasing sweet spots that suppress sensitivity to dephasing noise. We further exploit transmon asymmetry as a design parameter to access distinct noise-resilient operating regimes. These results establish an experimentally applicable framework for balancing gate speed, fidelity, and noise robustness while reducing characterization and recalibration overhead.

entry.title: Exceptional points and hysteresis in Kerr-Newman quasi-normal modes
entry.summary: Exceptional points (EPs) and eigenstate hysteresis, previously found in Kerr only with an auxiliary scalar field, arise intrinsically in the quasinormal-mode spectrum of Kerr-Newman black holes. Using a hyperboloidal formulation of the coupled gravito-electromagnetic Teukolsky equations and a Chebyshev pseudospectral method, we compute the $\ell=m=2$ spectrum and locate four EPs at up to $99.974\%$ of extremality, one from a new repulsion. The gaps close as a square root branch point, and quasistatic loops around one or more EPs exchange the coalescing modes, confirming hysteresis.

entry.title: Projective symmetry groups beyond spin-$1/2$: Classifying integer-spin quantum spin liquids
entry.summary: Wen's projective symmetry group (PSG), introduced a quarter of a century ago, reduced the classification of symmetric quantum spin liquids to an algebraic problem and has guided the study of spin-$1/2$ models and materials ever since. Many current candidate materials and quantum simulators, however, have spin-$1$ or larger moments, and no comparable classification exists for them. We formulate the PSG for fermionic partons of arbitrary spin $S$. Integer and half-odd-integer spins already differ in their gauge structure. Half-odd-integer spins give the familiar $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, $\mathrm{U}(1)$, and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant gauge groups, while integer spins give a different hierarchy that includes $\mathrm{U}(1)\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_2$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$; the latter has no spin-$1/2$ counterpart. Three lattice-independent results follow for integer spin. Singlet pairing of the partons is odd under site exchange. A lattice symmetry can exchange the particle and hole representations of the local constraint, which forces symmetry-related sites into opposite constraint sectors. And a time-reversal-symmetric $\mathrm{U}(1)$ state with the same constraint on every site can be gapped only if the number of sites per unit cell is a multiple of $2S+1$. We apply the formalism to the spin-$1$ diamond lattice, realized in frustrated A-site spinels, and find ten fully symmetric Ansätze up to second neighbors. In the $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg model at the mean-field level, the ground state depends on how the constraint is imposed. With the particle and hole representations, the lowest states are fully gapped $\mathrm{U}(1)$ states whose two sublattices sit in opposite constraint sectors, and one of them is gauge equivalent to a paired Ansatz. The classification provides a starting point for integer-spin quantum spin liquids on other lattices and in other materials.

entry.title: Electronic crystals and quasicrystals in semiconductor quantum wells: an AI-powered discovery
entry.summary: The homogeneous electron gas is a cornerstone of quantum condensed matter physics, providing the foundation for developing density functional theory and understanding electronic phases in semiconductors. However, theoretical understanding of strongly-correlated electrons in realistic semiconductor systems remains limited. In this work, we develop a neural network based variational approach to study quantum wells in three dimensional geometry for a variety of electron densities and well thicknesses. Starting from first principles, our unbiased AI-powered method reveals metallic and crystalline phases with both monolayer and bilayer charge distributions. In the emergent bilayer, we discover a new quantum phase of matter: the electronic quasicrystal.

entry.title: Testing Black Holes with Interstellar Missions: II. Flyby Probes
entry.summary: Recently, we demonstrated that while an interstellar mission to the nearest black hole remains highly speculative and extraordinarily challenging, it is not entirely implausible within the coming decades. Given that such a mission would likely take about a hundred years and require substantial financial and human investment, it is essential to assess whether it could investigate black holes and test General Relativity to a degree that cannot be achieved by Solar System observatories for the foreseeable future. In Paper I, we assumed the capability to decelerate the spacecraft and presented a preliminary study of how orbiting probes could test the nature of the compact object. In this second paper, we study how the black hole can be tested without decelerating the spacecraft, using flyby probes.

entry.title: Impact of non-standard neutrino-electron interactions on Big Bang Nucleosynthesis
entry.summary: Neutrino non-standard interactions (NSI) with electrons, predicted in many extended theoretical models of particle physics, are known to alter the picture of neutrino decoupling from the cosmic plasma. We update previous analyses of neutrino decoupling in the presence of NSI with electrons, extending the parameter space and assessing their impact on the primordial light-element abundances produced during Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN). We show that tracking the NSI-induced modifications of the neutrino distributions is necessary to accurately predict the helium-4 abundance, which cannot be derived from a pure $N_{\rm eff}$-driven change. BBN therefore provides additional observables that are complementary to $N_{\rm eff}$. We then derive cosmological constraints on non-universal and flavour-changing NSI parameters, using different dataset combinations, and compare them with bounds from terrestrial experiments. We find that the cosmological limits are significantly less stringent than the terrestrial ones, but they provide an independent probe of neutrino interactions in the early universe.

entry.title: Ultralight dark matter mixed with primordial black holes
entry.summary: Dark matter candidates span many orders of magnitude in mass, from ultralight bosonic fields to massive compact objects. In this work, we connect these two extremes by investigating ultralight dark matter (ULDM) mixed with primordial black holes (PBHs). We study mixed ULDM-PBH halos by separating the continuum PBH contribution from the shot-noise fluctuation generated by discrete PBHs. The continuum contribution enters the averaged Schrödinger-Poisson background, while the discreteness contribution is treated as a perturbation that induces ULDM eigenmode transitions and soliton heating. The two contributions have distinct parametric dependencies: continuum effects scale with PBH fraction, whereas discreteness-driven transition rates scale with the product of PBH fraction and individual PBH mass in the perturbative regime. For a fiducial mixed halo with ULDM particle mass $10^{-22}\,\mathrm{eV}$, virial mass of order $10^{10}\,M_{\odot}$, and PBH fraction $1\%$, the continuum PBH component modifies the background density, gravitational potential, and low-lying ULDM eigenvalues only at the sub-percent level. Nevertheless, this percent-level continuum PBH contribution produces a tens-of-percent response in the coherent soliton region, changing the radial mode participation by about $20\%$. For stellar-mass PBHs, the discrete shot-noise fluctuation induces extremely slow ULDM mode transitions, with the fastest low-lying multiplet transition having a timescale of order $10^9\,\mathrm{Gyr}$ for solar-mass PBHs. In this regime, the leading PBH effect is the continuum contribution, while discrete PBH shot noise is dynamically negligible on galactic timescales.

entry.title: Testing Black Holes with Interstellar Missions: I. Orbiting Probes
entry.summary: Recently, we showed that the possibility of an interstellar mission to the closest black hole, while highly speculative and extremely challenging, is not completely unrealistic within the next few decades. Since such a mission might last around a century and require significant financial and human resources, it is crucial to assess whether it can truly study black holes and test General Relativity at levels unattainable by observational facilities in the Solar System for many years. In this manuscript, we assume the capability to decelerate the spacecraft and present a preliminary study of how probes orbiting a black hole could test the nature of the compact object.

entry.title: Generalized Coordinate Bethe Ansatz and Quantum Integrability of the Time-Dependent Massive Thirring Model
entry.summary: We develop a generalized coordinate Bethe-ansatz framework for the massive Thirring model with an explicitly time-dependent fermion mass. Unlike the generalized Bethe ansatz for chiral quantum field theories, where particle transport acts in internal spin spaces and leads to quantum Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov equations, the present construction acts directly on particle coordinates and physical rapidities. Its central new feature is a rapidity lattice. Because the time-dependent mass couples right- and left-moving components already in the one-particle sector, a fixed-rapidity block is not closed under spatial winding. Periodicity therefore requires all sectors generated by the finite shift $β\toβ-p$. Particle exchange relates amplitudes on this lattice through scalar analytic difference equations of Ruijsenaars type, whose solutions determine the complete time-dependent many-body wavefunction. Consistency of the coordinate construction also selects an exponential evolution of the bare mass, providing a new realization of the time dependent integrability-renormalization group correspondence. In the static limit, the rapidity-lattice construction reduces to the conventional massive-Thirring Bethe equations. Through the massive-Thirring/sine Gordon equivalence, the result also connects this exact quantum construction to the generalized space-time dependent Lax formalism.

entry.title: Local tests of Schwarzschild-Bertotti-Robinson spacetime
entry.summary: We study weak field local tests of Schwarzschild-Bertotti-Robinson spacetime, which describes a static black hole embedded in an external magnetic field. Perihelion precession, deflection of light rays and time delay of radar echoes are the phenomena considered in this work to understand the possible effects of this external magnetic field on these observationally important tests. We not only derive weak field analytical results by employing appropriate methods, but also consider an exact approach to directly integrate the relevant geodesic equations, to both confirm those weak field analytical results and to obtain results beyond the weak field approximation.

entry.title: NTL amplification in a SuperCDMS-style detector fabricated from a University of South Dakota-grown germanium crystal
entry.summary: Neganov-Trofimov-Luke (NTL) amplification enables eV-sub-keV detection thresholds for low-mass dark-matter and coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering experiments. We evaluated two University of South Dakota (USD)-grown germanium crystals fabricated as SuperCDMS-style four-channel athermal-phonon detectors and operated near 10 mK. The crystals had electrically active impurity concentrations near $10^10~\mathrm^-3$ and etch-pit densities of $300$-$7000~\mathrm^-2$. Contact-free biasing produced no resolvable amplification. However, after depositing a 600 nm aluminum bias contact, Detector~2 exhibited clear voltage-dependent NTL gain. The reconstructed channel-B energy increased from approximately 3.9 keV at 0 V to 34.9 keV at 40 V, corresponding to an 8.9-fold enhancement. Statistical centroid uncertainties were below 0.3%, while low-bias fits yielded effective prompt- and NTL-phonon response coefficients of $(6.77\pm0.82)%$ and $(4.77\pm0.20)%$, respectively, excluding systematic uncertainties. These results demonstrate the feasibility of USD-grown germanium for SuperCDMS-style high-voltage phonon detectors and highlight the importance of both crystal quality and contact fabrication in achieving NTL amplification.

entry.title: Gravitational Waves from New Inflation
entry.summary: Gravitational waves provide one of the most powerful observational probes for discriminating among inflationary models. In particular, it has recently become clear that the high-frequency gravitational-wave spectrum encodes a wealth of information about the properties of the inflaton and the post-inflationary dynamics. In this paper, we present the first comprehensive prediction of the complete gravitational-wave spectrum in the new inflation scenario, a prototypical realization of small-field inflation, incorporating all known production mechanisms including both the classical and quantum sources.

entry.title: The diversity of late-time interaction in Type II supernovae
entry.summary: Studying core-collapse supernovae (SNe) beyond one year after explosion, when ejecta interaction with circumstellar material (CSM) progressively becomes the dominant power source, offers critical insights into the progenitor mass loss history. Using binary progenitors that underwent different levels of H-rich envelope stripping, we present radiative transfer calculations of the ejecta with CSM interaction in Type IIb, II-L and II-P SN scenarios covering epochs of 1.5 to 3-6yr, with a focus on the UV and optical properties. The impact of CSM interaction is evaluated for a cold-dense shell (CDS) of 0.1-2.0Msun (CDS velocity of ~5000-10000km/s) and shock powers of 1e39-1e41erg/s, producing a grid of about 200 models. We find that Lyalpha, MgII2800, and Halpha are typically the strongest individual lines, MgII2800 being the most constant relative to changes in time and in CDS mass. Lyalpha thrives at low CDS mass and is strongly attenuated otherwise. A large fraction of the emerging UV and optical flux is, however, influenced by a forest of Fe lines, which introduces strong optical depth effects. A myriad of other lines, generally forbidden, are predicted that each contain less than a percent of the total flux. N enrichment yield stronger N lines in the UV and optical. A subset of these models roughly match UV and optical observations of SNe 1993J, 1998S, 2013ej, and 2023ixf at 1.5-3yr, although matching the full range consistently is a challenge, in particular when dust must be invoked. Blue-red asymmetry of line profiles is typical of all lines in the UV, the more so at earlier times or higher CDS mass, even in the absence of dust. In our simulations, optical depth effects, associated with the gas or dust or both, quenches the emission of Lyalpha or [OIII]4958-5007A from regions within or below the CDS.

entry.title: Carrollian Symmetries and Dynamical Entropy
entry.summary: Carrollian geometry has recently emerged as the proper language to understand the geometry of null hypersurfaces from an intrinsic perspective. In this paper, we demonstrate that the Noether charge associated with the intrinsic conformal symmetry of Carrollian manifolds yields exactly the dynamical entropy formula recently proposed by Hollands, Wald and Zhang. This result follows directly from the requirement that the gravitational phase space induced on a finite distance null hypersurface be anomaly-free, in a covariant phase space sense. We then show that a linearized perturbation of this dynamical entropy charge, sourced by an external matter perturbation falling across the hypersurface, satisfies a physical process first law. Moreover, upon imposing the classical null energy condition, a linearized second law holds for the dynamical entropy. We then turn to a semi-classical generalization of this construction, where we argue that a notion of dynamical generalized entropy follows from considering perturbations sourced by external quantum matter. By imposing the quantum null energy condition (QNEC), we find a generalized second law for a linearized perturbation of the dynamical generalized entropy. Finally, we use our results to speculate on relations to the quantum focusing conjecture.

entry.title: Rotation slows the instability of Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes
entry.summary: We present nonlinear 3+1 evolutions of rotating Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes. We construct stationary rotating drainhole solutions with a spectral solver up to an equatorial rotation velocity of 99% of the speed of light, validate the solver against published symmetric solutions, and correct an inconsistency in a published field equation. Perturbed only by truncation error, the evolutions show that rotation slows the radial instability of the static wormhole. Near 30% of the extremal angular momentum the unperturbed throat expands instead of collapsing, rather than the instability disappearing as second-order perturbation theory suggests. From 58% upward we find no evidence of instability over the evolved times; at the fastest spin this holds at three resolutions. Collapsing rotating throats emit an axisymmetric quadrupolar gravitational-wave burst whose energy grows with spin. Second-order perturbative initial data trigger the instability through their own truncation error, so they are unsuitable for stability studies.

entry.title: PBR sensitivity to boosted dark matter explanation for the KM3-230213A event
entry.summary: POEMMA-Balloon with Radio (PBR) is a hybrid fluorescence and optical Cherenkov telescope that is a pathfinder instrument for a future Probe Of Extreme Multi-Messenger Astrophysics (POEMMA), together with a radio instrument, to be flown on a super pressure balloon in Spring 2028. One of its science objectives is follow up of astrophysical event alerts via signals of tau decays in the atmosphere, sourced by Earth-skimming tau neutrinos. The recent report of the KM3NeT Collaboration's muon event with $ E_μ=120^{+110}_{-60}$ PeV sparked searches for beyond the standard model (BSM) physics explanations. Using a specific, boosted dark matter scenario which together with the KM3NeT observation, sets a scale for the fluence of boosted dark matter in this energy range, we assess the capabilities of PBR to constrain or discover such a source for a boosted dark matter energy spectrum above $\sim 10^8$ GeV. PBR has discovery potential for dark matter energies above $10^9$ GeV, and depending on BSM input parameters, to dark matter energies as low as $1.5\times 10^8$ GeV. While the analysis is focused on one BSM example, the methodology is applicable to any BSM physics that affects tau production in the Earth.

entry.title: Constraining Dynamical Dark Energy with Tomographic Galaxy and CMB Weak Lensing Through Higher-Order Statistics
entry.summary: Tomographic weak gravitational lensing probes cosmic structure growth and geometry, making it a powerful probe of dynamical dark energy. We forecast information beyond the lensing power spectrum from non-Gaussian statistics of tomographic galaxy and CMB lensing convergence maps. Using the $\texttt{DDELenS}$ suite of ray-traced $N$-body simulations, we build Gaussian process emulators for power spectra, Minkowski functionals, moments, peak and minima counts, and the wavelet scattering transform, varying $Ω_m$, $σ_8$, $w_0$, and $w_a$. We consider Rubin-like galaxy lensing and Simons Observatory-like CMB lensing over $15{,}000\,\mathrm{deg}^2$, and validate the analysis using a withheld fiducial cosmology, analytical power-spectrum forecasts, and Gaussian random-field null tests. As an initial step, we neglect baryonic effects and intrinsic alignments and approximate galaxy sources as discrete redshift planes. Using all source redshifts at $z_s=\{0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 1100\}$, combining all five non-Gaussian statistics reduces uncertainties on $w_0$ and $w_a$ by $24.3\%$ and $28.0\%$, and on $Ω_m$ and $σ_8$ by $41.9\%$ and $45.8\%$, relative to the power-spectrum-only baseline. The resulting $w_0$ and $w_a$ uncertainties are $34.7\%$ and $48.7\%$ smaller than current DESI+DES constraints. If the DESI+DES best-fit values remain unchanged, this precision would increase the significance of the departure from $Λ$CDM from $3.0σ$ to $5.2σ$, compared with $3.8σ$ from the power spectrum alone, assuming a Gaussian posterior and unchanged $w_0$--$w_a$ correlation. Minkowski functionals and moments provide comparable constraining power, while combining them with the other summaries gives the strongest constraints. Broad galaxy-lensing redshift coverage is particularly important for dynamical dark energy, while CMB lensing provides complementary information.

entry.title: Primordial black hole formation in bulk-viscous cosmology
entry.summary: We investigate primordial black hole (PBH) formation in a cosmological background with bulk viscosity. Using numerical simulations, we determine the collapse threshold and the resulting PBH mass. We find that the critical threshold $μ_c$ retains a dependence on the equation-of-state parameter $w$ similar to that in the inviscid case, but is enhanced by an amount comparable to the bulk-viscosity strength $ε$. For fixed $w$, the increase in $μ_c$ is approximately linear in $ε$. By fitting the standard critical-scaling law for near-threshold collapse, we find that the bulk viscosity leads to an enhancement in the resulting PBH mass. These results indicate that bulk viscosity can systematically modify both the PBH threshold and PBH mass scaling law in the early Universe.

entry.title: Deep Learning Search for Gravitational Waves from Compact Binary Coalescence
entry.summary: Gravitational-wave searches rely on a combination of methods, including matched filtering, coherent analyses, and more recent machine-learning-based pipelines. For compact binary coalescences --- where signals originate from the relativistic dynamics of compact objects --- matched filtering remains a central element, but its computational cost will increase substantially with the data volumes and parameter-space coverage required by next-generation interferometers such as the Einstein Telescope. Developing complementary strategies that reduce computational load while preserving detection performance is therefore essential. We investigate a hybrid approach that combines matched-filtering concepts with Convolutional Neural Networks, enabling efficient signal searches without relying on the usual $χ^2$ rejection test. Using simulated data sets that include injected signals in Gaussian noise, transient noise, and physical effects not represented in the template bank --- such as eccentricity, precession and higher-order modes --- we show that the method achieves a detection efficiency comparable to or better than a standard matched-filtering search while offering a more resource-efficient pipeline in all the cases where the physics included in the signals were not represented in the template bank or when glitches were affecting the data. Conversely, the analysis also reveals some loss of detection capability for standard BNS/BBH searches in pure Gaussian noise. These results indicate that deep-learning-assisted searches can support sustainable gravitational-wave data analysis in future detector eras.

entry.title: Cosmic Ray Observations using Coincident Scintillator and Radio Signals with the Beamforming Elevated Array for COsmic Neutrinos (BEACON)
entry.summary: At energies above 100 PeV, coherent radio frequency (RF) emission across the 10 -- 1000 MHz band from cosmic particle-induced atmospheric showers becomes increasingly dominant, making radio detection a powerful probe at ultrahigh energies. The Beamforming Elevated Array for COsmic Neutrinos (BEACON) considers mountaintop phased radio arrays to monitor large areas at the horizon for upward-going geomagnetic emission in the 30 -- 80 MHz band produced as a consequence of Earth-skimming tau neutrinos. As part of ongoing efforts to measure the sensitivity of BEACON to such signals, the BEACON prototype identifies cosmic rays through the same emission mechanism. Prior to 2023, BEACON operated a four-antenna prototype, which successfully demonstrated identification of coherent and impulsive sources using a beamforming RF trigger. In 2023, we upgraded the instrument to six newly designed antennas and added an independent scintillator array to cross-validate radio-detectable cosmic rays. This work details the observation of 22 candidate cosmic-ray events in a scintillator-coincidence-triggered dataset using selection cuts based on expected radio characteristics. A simulation of the hybrid-instrument performance verifies this observation rate to within an order of magnitude. We estimate a background of 0.11 events by applying the selection cuts to synthetic datasets of uncorrelated radio-scintillator pairs that are randomly formed using fixed-rate software-triggered data. The reconstructed signal polarization angles are consistent with pure geomagnetic emission compared to various background classes.

entry.title: In-orbit anomaly and recovery of IXPE detector 2
entry.summary: The Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE) is a joint NASA-ASI mission launched in December 2021 to measure the linear polarization of celestial X-ray sources in the 2-8 keV energy range. The payload comprises three identical telescopes, each combining grazing-incidence X-ray optics with a focal-plane photoelectric polarimeter based on the Gas Pixel Detector technology. On 14 April 2025, the second detector experienced an anomaly that significantly altered the electrical behavior of the ASIC responsible for reading out the photoelectron track images. In this contribution, we describe the effect of the anomaly on the instrumental response and the actions taken to mitigate its effects and recover the scientific observations of the instrument.

entry.title: Compact representation of strongly correlated Green's functions: the MOR+EC way to explore phase space
entry.summary: Repeated evaluation of the single-particle Green's function (GF) across parameter space is a recurring bottleneck in many-body methods, limiting the resolution at which phase boundaries may be probed and the frequency resolution of computed spectra. We introduce MOR+EC, a framework that constructs reusable reduced-order models for computing single-particle Green's functions by combining eigenvector continuation (EC) for parameter space exploration and model order reduction (MOR) for extrapolation in frequency space. Contrary to conventional parameterized MOR, we construct these reduced-order models with a parameter-independent resolvent, further reducing the number of required full-space evaluations. Benchmarking against exact diagonalization as the impurity solver for our example case of DMFT calculations for single- and two-band models, MOR+EC reproduces the DMFT-converged impurity GF to an average relative error below $10^{-3}$, with a median wall-time speedup of $9.5$-$92\times$. This accuracy and efficiency together resolve a fine-grained scan of the impurity occupation as doping is tuned and produce a high-resolution phase diagram of an orbital-selective Mott transition. The reduced-order model also reproduces real- and imaginary-frequency spectra at no additional cost in full-space evaluations. This framework applies broadly to GF-based methods requiring repeated parametric evaluation and high resolution of the frequency axis.

entry.title: Stabilizing and detecting electron fractionalization in the Hofstadter-Hubbard model
entry.summary: Motivated by the recent progress in correlated Chern insulator physics in moiré systems, we investigate the half-filled triangular-lattice Hofstadter--Hubbard model and its electron fractionalization. Among various competing non-magnetic states, increasing the orbital flux stabilizes and broadens the $\mathrm{U}(1)_2$ chiral spin liquid phase in the Mott regime. In this exotic regime, the electron is fractionalized into gapped spinons and gapped chargons, whose effective bands are linked to the orbital flux. The convolution of the narrow spinon bands with the gapped chargon excitations produces rich and discernible structures in the electron spectral function and the density of states. These results not only identify the orbital flux as a control parameter for the detailed patterns of electron fractionalization and the nature of the Mott transition, but also provide the key spectral characteristics for the angle-resolved photoemission and scanning tunneling studies of the relevant systems, linking the free-particle band topology to intrinsic topological order in the correlated regime.

entry.title: Asymptotic limits in class-$\mathcal{S}$ theories and non-Abelian Hodge theory
entry.summary: We develop a non-Abelian Hodge-theoretic refinement of asymptotic limits in type-$A$ class-$\mathcal S$ theories, enriching the geometric description of the degenerating UV curve with gauge-theoretic data encoded by the associated Hitchin system. A degeneration of the UV curve produces a long plumbing tube, which we equip with the local monodromy data of a Hitchin-Simpson flat connection admitting a regular-singular logarithmic model. The semisimple and unipotent parts of the monodromy govern, respectively, the power-law and logarithmic growth of flat sections through the tube. Combining this non-Abelian holonomy with the geometric Picard-Lefschetz monodromy yields a decorated cusp label that incorporates Higgs-bundle information and extends tube-wise to intersections of boundary divisors. We also discuss a particular class of monodromy labels for which the weak gauge algebra specified by the fixture and gluing data lies in the reductive monodromy centralizer. In type $A$, we organize the local monodromy labels into discrete types specified by the eigenspace multiplicities of the semisimple part and the Jordan type of the nilpotent logarithm of the unipotent part. Finally, we illustrate the construction for $SL(3,\mathbb C)$ on the four-punctured sphere and $SL(4,\mathbb C)$ on the two-punctured torus.

entry.title: Testing Dynamical Dark-Energy Model with Standard Sirens
entry.summary: Bright standard sirens from the Einstein Telescope (ET) provide an independent probe of cosmic expansion. In this article, we test whether future ET observations can constrain a dynamical dark-energy scenario inspired by DESI DR2. Using the best-fitting 29-bin dark-energy equation of state as the fiducial cosmology, we generate mock catalogs of 100, 500, 1000, and 3000 binary-neutron-star standard sirens with known host redshifts, and reconstruct the equation of state using both GW-only data and combined analyses with DESI DR2 BAO, BBN, and a compressed CMB constraint. The effective numbers of constrained modes are $N_{\mathrm{eff}}\sim 4-5$ (GW-only) and $5-6$ (combined), with information concentrated in a few correlated modes. The GW3000 catalog yields a departure from $Λ$CDM exceeding $5σ$, and combined analyses reach similar significance for $O(10^3)$ events. Comparing flat $Λ$CDM with its Chevallier-Polarski-Linder extension using GW data alone gives significances of $3.3σ$ and $6.3σ$ for 1000 and 3000 events, rising to $7.7σ$ and $11.0σ$ with external data. These results indicate that a few thousand ET bright standard sirens could provide a sensitive test of departures from $Λ$CDM.

entry.title: Unambiguous determination of the THz conductivity in driven YBa$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{6+x}$
entry.summary: Mid-infrared pump, THz probe experiments in YBa$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{6+x}$ yield evidence of a high-temperature transient state of the material with the optical properties of a superconductor. However, there are ambiguities in the extracted transient c-axis THz optical properties, primarily resulting from the sublinear growth of the THz response with increasing mid-infrared pump fluence. It was proposed that this effect may be related to saturation of the material's response, which would then perturb its spatial profile and lead one to overestimate the induced change in the transient optical properties. Yet, sublinear growth of the signal could also arise from other effects unrelated to saturation, for example from a change in reflectivity or deposition depth for the pump pulses. Here, we remove this ambiguity by experimentally measuring the fluence-dependent complex optical constants at the 15-20 THz frequencies of the pump. We show that the observed sublinear growth is to be attributed in large part to the enhanced reflection and reduced penetration depth of the pump field at high fluences. When taking into account these findings, we confirm the original interpretation of a light-induced superconducting state both qualitatively and quantitatively.

entry.title: Efficient Eccentric Effective-One-Body Dynamics via Near-Identity Averaging Transformations
entry.summary: Next-generation gravitational-wave detectors, such as LISA, the Einstein Telescope, and Cosmic Explorer, will require accurate and efficient models of long-lived black hole binary signals, including those with significant eccentricity. A challenge for eccentric effective-one-body models is the cost of resolving rapidly oscillating orbital dynamics over the inspiral, particularly for low-mass and large-mass-ratio systems. We address this by recasting the nonspinning eccentric effective-one-body equations of motion in terms of osculating orbital elements and then applying near-identity averaging transformations to eliminate the fast orbital-timescale structure during the inspiral. Each order in this procedure suppresses the oscillatory behavior by one factor of the ratio of orbital to radiation-reaction timescales. The resulting averaged dynamics are evolved on the radiation-reaction timescale, and then the system is mapped back to the full EOB dynamics for the final transition to plunge. This reduces the cost of the inspiral dynamics by up to two orders of magnitude, eliminating this as the primary bottleneck for long waveforms. The overall waveform-generation speedup spans $1.5 - 8 \times$, motivating the development of more efficient waveform-generation methods. We also validate the accuracy of the method by comparing waveforms generated from the averaged and full effective-one-body dynamics across a broad region of parameter space for moderate to large eccentricities. Carrying out this averaging procedure to next-to-next-to-leading order is needed to accurately model comparable-mass binaries, yielding mismatches $\leq 8.05 \times 10^{-5}$. These results establish near-identity averaging as a practical route to efficient eccentric effective-one-body inspirals, and provide a foundation for further extensions to low-eccentricity and spinning waveform models.
